titulo: What the agent sees: accessibility tree × screenshot
lead: You see colors, a yellow button, and a date field. A browser agent like Playwright MCP gets something else: a list of roles and names, the accessibility tree. In this lesson you print that tree for the example page, compare it with the screenshot, and learn to read what's missing.
objetivo: read the accessibility tree the agent receives and compare it with the screenshot of the same page.

aprende.t: Role and name: the two things the agent looks for
The page tree printed by the kit
The gaps: a control with no name, a div pretending to be a button
Tree as text × screen as pixels

hero_alt: Dark monitor showing a form page, with thin outlines of boxes over it that reveal the page structure.

nos.detalhe: What you see. To work from the screen alone, the model would have to read the image and guess where each control is. The example page's screenshot is about 15 thousand bytes of PNG.

The browser builds the accessibility tree from the HTML: each control becomes a role (textbox, combobox, button) with a name. Screen readers use it, and a snapshot of it is what Playwright MCP hands to the model. On the example page, that's 182 bytes of text.
The model reads the tree and decides: "fill in the Seu nome field, pick Serviço, click Agendar". If a control has no name, it has no safe way to choose it.
The tool performs the action on the chosen control, using the reference from the tree (in agent-browser, for example, refs like @e2). Then it reads the tree again to see the result.

secoes.volta: After the action, a new tree
secoes.legenda: Anything that isn't in the tree with a role and a name, the agent can only find by guessing from the screen.

texto: textbox is a text field, combobox is a list of options, button is a button, link is a link, heading is a title, img is an image. The role comes from the HTML element: input, select, button, a, h1, img.
A div with onclick doesn't become a button: it shows up as loose text.
The name appears in quotes: textbox "Seu nome". It comes from the label, from aria-label, from the image's alt, or from the button's text.
No quotes means the control has no name: - textbox, - img.

exemplo.rot: A catch on the example page
exemplo.texto: In antes.html the first field shows up as textbox "Seu nome", but the name comes only from the placeholder. It disappears when the person types, and it isn't a label: the test in lesson 1 got stuck on exactly this field.

texto: main and a level-1 heading tell you where the main content is. Without them, the tree is a flat list and the agent can't tell what's the menu and what's the task.

secoes.titulo: The tree for antes.html, next to the screen
secoes.sub: arvore.mjs opens the page in a headless Chromium, prints the tree with Playwright 1.63.0's locator.ariaSnapshot() (the same snapshot format Playwright MCP uses), saves the screenshot, and checks what's missing.

abas.html:
## árvore de acessibilidade · 9 linhas · 182 bytes
- text: Agendar revisão
- img
- textbox "Seu nome"
- combobox:
  - option "Escolha" [selected]
  - option "Revisão básica"
  - option "Revisão completa"
- textbox
- text: Agendar
## tela · /tmp/tela-antes.png · 14536 bytes (o modelo teria de ler pixels)
## conferência · http://127.0.0.1:PORTA/antes.html
  - img sem nome acessível
  - combobox sem nome acessível
  - textbox sem nome acessível
  - <html> sem lang
  - sem <main>
  - sem <h1>
  - <div> clicável que não é botão ("Agendar")
  - campo #nome sem <label> (só placeholder)
  - campo #servico sem <label>
  - campo #data sem <label>
problemas: 10
saída: 1

Nine lines of tree versus 14,536 bytes of PNG. In the tree, the service list (combobox), the date field, and the image have no name, and the "Agendar" button became text. The check lists 10 problems and the script exits with 1.

abas.rot: Common mistake: "it has a name, so it's fine"
abas.html: The line textbox "Seu nome" looks good. But the check flags campo #nome sem <label> (só placeholder): Chromium uses the placeholder as a last resort for the name. The lesson 1 test looks the field up by its label (getByLabel) and got stuck right there. A real label is <label for>.

secoes.sub: The tree of the example page and the tree of your site.

exercicios.texto: Run the "tree and screen" block. Open /tmp/tela-antes.png and, for each line of the tree, find the control in the image. Mark the ones that have no name.
exercicios.pronto: node arvore.mjs antes --tela /tmp/tela-antes.png → problemas: 10 and saída: 1, and the file /tmp/tela-antes.png exists.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · The tree of your site
exercicios.texto: Run arvore.mjs on the same page of your site that you used in lesson 1. Write down the number of problems: it comes back in lesson 3 and in the plan.
exercicios.pronto: node arvore.mjs https://[your-site]/[page] ends with problemas: N and saída: 0 (N = 0) or saída: 1, with N noted down.

perguntas.p: What does Playwright MCP hand to the model so it can decide where to click?
opcoes: A PNG screenshot at every step of the task
The entire source code of the page, with the CSS and JavaScript
A snapshot of the accessibility tree
The list of WebMCP tools registered by the page
perguntas.explica: Playwright MCP uses accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots. WebMCP tools are a different approach (calling), and they only exist with an origin trial.

perguntas.p: The tree shows "- textbox" with nothing after it. What does that tell you?
opcoes: That the text field has no accessible name
That the field was filled in by the agent and is locked
perguntas.explica: The name appears in quotes. Without quotes, the agent has no way to know whether that field is the date, the phone, or the email.

perguntas.p: Does a button made with a div and onclick show up in the tree as a button?
opcoes: As button, the same as a button made with button
As link, because the div is clickable
As combobox with the Agendar option
As loose text, with no button role
perguntas.explica: The role comes from the HTML element. A div with onclick is text to the tree; for the agent, there is no button to click by name.

perguntas.p: The field has only the placeholder "Seu nome" and the tree shows textbox "Seu nome". Is it solved?
opcoes: Yes: if it shows up with a name in the tree, the agent always finds it
No: the name comes from the placeholder; the label is missing
Yes, as long as the page has main and h1
No: a placeholder stops the agent from submitting the form
perguntas.explica: Chromium uses the placeholder as a last resort. It disappears when you type, and anyone who looks for the label (like the lesson 1 test) won't find it.

itens.texto: The browser agent reads roles and names, a short list of text.
A control with no name is a control the agent has to guess.
It gives a name in the tree, but it is not a label; use label.
